title: Google loses fight against EU’s record $4.7B fine over alleged antitrust practices
facts: The European Union's top court dismissed Google's appeal of a 2018 European Commission antitrust ruling.
The European Union imposed a $4.7 billion antitrust fine on Google.
The European Commission accused Google of anti-competitive practices relating to the promotion of Google Search and Chrome on Android devices.
Shares in Alphabet, the parent company of Google, fell 1.3% following the EU court's decision.
The EU court ruling ended an eight-year-long legal battle between Google and European regulators.
Google has no further ability to appeal the $4.7 billion European Union antitrust decision.
Google adapted its agreements in 2018 to comply with the European Commission's initial decision.
The initial European Union fine imposed on Google for Android-related practices was 4.34 billion euros.
The European Union lowered the initial Android-related antitrust fine to 4.1 billion euros.
The European Union fined Google 3 billion euros ($3.45 billion) in 2025 for alleged self-preferencing practices in its advertising technology business.
US President Donald Trump threatened to impose 100% tariffs on French wine if France maintained a 3% tax on US tech giants.
US President Donald Trump stated he warned French President Emmanuel Macron about potential retaliatory tariffs.
The French 3% tax targeted US technology companies including Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Apple.
US President Donald Trump threatened a 100% tariff on any country implementing a digital services tax on US firms.
European countries including the UK, Spain, Italy, Austria, and Denmark have adopted digital service taxes.
